raw_response:
I've been farming these same 9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. I'm 64, and it's just my wife and me at home these days — our children found work in the city. With only two of us and our ages, I have to think carefully about what we can physically manage and what we must hire out. I've stuck with cotton on all 9 mu because I know this crop inside and out, and honestly, at my age the frantic harvest turnaround of wheat-maize double cropping would break us. Cotton gives us a longer, more manageable harvest window.

I'm planting in mid-to-late April, once the soil temperature steadies. I've bought improved hybrid seed at about 50 yuan per mu — about 2 kg per mu. I learned long ago that saved seed is false economy for cotton; the boll size and disease resistance of hybrid seed pay for themselves. For fertilizer, I'm putting down a base of compound fertilizer before planting — roughly 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 — and I'll topdress with urea at flowering and boll-setting in July, bringing my total nitrogen to about 14 kg per mu. I keep it at that level because I've seen the diminishing returns on this land. The extension station tests also showed my phosphorus running low, so I'm making sure to get about 6 kg P₂O₅ and 5 kg K₂O per mu into the soil this year.

I have well water, but pumping is metered and costly. I'll irrigate twice — once at planting if the spring is dry, and once critically at flowering in July. A third time only if the drought is severe. For pests, cotton bollworm is my main enemy. I plan 4 to 5 insecticide sprays and a pre-emergence herbicide; hand-weeding 9 mu with just two old people is impossible. The chemical cost runs me about 170 yuan per mu.

Labor is my biggest headache and my biggest expense. My wife and I can handle fertilizing, spraying, and some of the early picking — maybe 45 family days between us. But planting and the three to four rounds of cotton picking in September and October require hired hands. I'll need about 85 days of hired labor at roughly 120 yuan per day. That's over 10,000 yuan in cash, my single largest outlay, but there's no alternative.

If the weather is normal, I'm expecting about 300 kg of lint per mu. Last year I got 280 kg, but the winter soil moisture was better this time and I've adjusted my topdress timing. At about 15 yuan per kg for lint, that's roughly 40,500 yuan gross. After my total input and labor costs of about 14,900 yuan, I should clear around 25,000 yuan. It won't make us rich, but for two old people in the village, it's enough to live on, pay for any medicine, and sleep without worry.
